name: Honduras
description: Honduras offers expats an appealing blend of vibrant culture, warm climate, and a significantly lower cost of living compared to Western countries. While security concerns exist, dedicated expat communities in areas like Roatán, Tegucigalpa, and San Pedro Sula enjoy a manageable day-to-day life with improving safety profiles. The country's territorial tax system is a key draw for those with foreign-sourced income.
longdescription: Expat life in Honduras is characterized by a rich cultural experience and a relaxed pace, particularly in the coastal and island regions. The economy, while developing, offers affordability that can significantly enhance an expat's lifestyle. Major cities like Tegucigalpa and San Pedro Sula provide more amenities and job opportunities, while the Bay Islands (Roatán, Utila) are popular for their English-speaking communities, natural beauty, and tourism-focused lifestyle. Despite a historical reputation for high crime rates, recent government crackdowns and improved coordination have led to a substantial decline in violence, especially in expat-heavy zones. The cost of living is notably lower than in North America or Europe, with housing, groceries, and domestic services being particularly affordable. Access to private healthcare facilities in major cities is improving, offering services comparable to mid-tier Western standards. While Spanish is the official language, English is widely spoken in tourist areas like the Bay Islands. The society is generally welcoming, though adapting to local customs and bureaucratic processes can be a challenge for newcomers.

visas.name: Honduras Retirement Visa
visas.description: Honduras residency for retirees with a pension or regular income. One of the most affordable retirement destinations in Central America with a Bay Islands expat community.
benefits: Very low cost of living
Bay Islands diving and beaches
Year-round warm climate
Tax exemptions on imported goods
Renewable residence
visas.path_to_residency_description: After 3 years of legal residency, eligible to apply for permanent residency.
required_documents: Passport
Proof of income ($1,500+/month)
Birth certificate (apostilled)
Police clearance (apostilled)
Medical certificate

visas.name: Residencia Pensionado (Retirement Visa)
visas.description: The 'Residencia Pensionado' visa in Honduras allows retired foreign nationals to reside permanently in the country based on a stable, lifetime pension or retirement income from abroad. This visa provides a pathway to long-term residency and eventual citizenship in Honduras.
visas.target_applicant: Ideal applicants are retirees receiving a permanent and stable pension from a government or private institution outside Honduras.
visas.path_to_residency_description: The Residencia Pensionado initially grants temporary residency which leads to permanent residency. After three years of continuous legal residency, applicants are eligible to apply for Honduran citizenship, provided they demonstrate basic Spanish language ability and maintain a clean criminal record.
visas.renewal_conditions: Maintaining the minimum income threshold and complying with Honduran immigration laws, including not being absent for more than 12 consecutive months (a single day visit per year is sufficient to maintain residency). The physical residence card may require periodic renewal.
visas.tax_implications: Honduras operates a territorial tax system. Foreign-sourced pension income is exempt from Honduran income tax. Only income generated within Honduras is subject to local taxation. Residents may also benefit from exemptions on import duties for household goods and a personal vehicle.
benefits: Permanent residency in Honduras.
Eligibility for Honduran citizenship after 3 years of residency.
Exemption from income tax on foreign-sourced pension income.
Exoneration from import duties and sales tax on household goods (menaje de casa) and a personal vehicle.
Minimal physical presence requirement to maintain residency (one day per year).
required_documents: Application addressed to the Secretary of State in the Offices of Human Rights, Justice, Governance, and Decentralization.
Power of Attorney for legal representative.
Recent passport-sized photograph (6cm x 5cm).
Certificate of Migratory Movements issued by the National Institute of Migration.
Criminal record certificate from country of origin and last residence, duly authenticated/apostilled.
Certificate of no criminal complaints from the Honduran Dirección Policial de Investigación (DPI).
Medical certificate (not older than 6 months).
Authenticated photocopy of passport.
Certificate from the institution issuing the permanent and stable pension, proving an income of no less than $1,500.00 USD per month or its equivalent in national currency.
Evidence that the pension will be received in a Honduran financial institution.
Bank reference indicating the pension will be transferred.
Official translation of all foreign documents into Spanish by the Ministry of Foreign Affairs or Honduran Consulates.
application_process_steps: Gather all required documents, ensuring foreign documents are apostilled/legalized and officially translated into Spanish.
Appoint a licensed Honduran immigration attorney to represent the applicant.

Submit the application and all supporting documents to the Secretary of State in the Offices of Human Rights, Justice, Governance, and Decentralization, possibly initiated via a Honduran consulate abroad or in-country if already present.
Pay the application fee.
Await the administrative resolution of the application.
Upon approval, register with the National Registry of Foreigners at the National Institute of Migration and obtain the foreign resident identification card.

visas.name: Residencia Rentista (Independent Means / Passive Income Visa)
visas.description: The Residencia Rentista program in Honduras is a visa designed for foreign nationals who can demonstrate a stable and permanent passive income generated from sources outside Honduras or within the country. It allows individuals to live in Honduras without requiring local employment, making it suitable for those who are financially independent.
visas.target_applicant: Ideal applicants are retirees, digital nomads, investors, or individuals with passive income from sources such as rentals, dividends, bonds, or other investments, seeking an affordable residency with a path to citizenship.
visas.path_to_residency_description: The Residencia Rentista initially grants temporary residency, typically for two years, which is indefinitely renewable. After five years of continuous legal residency, applicants are eligible for permanent residency. Furthermore, applicants may apply for Honduran citizenship after three years of continuous legal residency.
visas.renewal_conditions: The applicant must maintain the required monthly income threshold and continue to meet the conditions of the residency.
visas.tax_implications: Honduras operates under a territorial tax system. This means that income generated from foreign sources, such as rentals, dividends, or investments from abroad, is generally exempt from Honduran income tax. Residents are only taxed on income earned within Honduras.
benefits: No investment or donation required
Path to Honduran citizenship after 3 years of residency
Allows dual/multiple citizenship (in practice)
Territorial tax system, exempting foreign-sourced income from Honduran tax
Unrestricted movement within the CA-4 zone (Honduras, Guatemala, El Salvador, Nicaragua)
required_documents: Application addressed to the Secretary of State in the Offices of Government, Justice and Decentralization
Fiscal stamps (timbres) of Lps. 100.00 for each applicant
Contact address and phone number of residence in Honduras
Authenticated Power of Attorney (Carta Poder) for a legal representative (lawyer)
Two recent passport-sized photographs (6cm high x 5cm wide), with name on the back
Original certificate of migratory movement from the National Institute of Migration (INM)
Original entry request authorized by a Honduran Consul (if applying from abroad; not needed if already in Honduras)
Criminal record certificate from the country of origin, duly legalized/apostilled and officially translated into Spanish
Certificate of no criminal record from the Supreme Court of Justice of Honduras
Certificate of no police complaints or records from the Dirección Policial de Investigación (DPI) of Honduras
Medical certificate issued by a professional from the Honduran Medical College, not older than six months
Authenticated photocopy of a valid passport

Proof of permanent, lawful, and stable income (US$2,500 monthly) from abroad or within Honduras, authenticated by a Public Notary and the Chamber of Notaries of the province of residence, and evidence that the income will be received through a national financial institution in Honduras
Birth certificate, legalized/apostilled and officially translated into Spanish (if applicable)
application_process_steps: Gather and prepare all required documents from the home country, ensuring they are apostilled/legalized and officially translated into Spanish.
Hire a local Honduran attorney (apoderado legal) to represent the applicant and file the initial residency application with the National Institute of Migration (INM).
Submit the completed application along with all supporting documentation and proof of income to the INM.
Upon approval of the administrative resolution, proceed to register with the National Registry of Foreigners at the INM to obtain the resident identification card.

visas.name: Residencia Inversionista (Investor Visa)
visas.description: The 'Residencia Inversionista' program in Honduras is for foreign nationals who wish to invest capital in any lawful economic activity within Honduras or in certificates, securities, or bonds issued by the Honduran state and national financial institutions. This visa grants permanent residency, allowing the investor to reside in the country without requiring frequent visa renewals.
visas.target_applicant: Ideal applicants are foreign investors seeking long-term residency in Honduras by investing in the country's legitimate economic sectors or government/financial instruments.
visas.path_to_residency_description: The 'Residencia Inversionista' directly grants permanent residency in Honduras. After a period of permanent residency, it may lead to eligibility for citizenship according to Honduran nationality laws.
visas.renewal_conditions: The residency is granted as permanent from its inception. Conditions for maintaining permanent residency would typically include adhering to Honduran laws and maintaining the investment.
visas.tax_implications: Standard Honduran resident tax rules apply. There are no specific tax exemptions for 'Residencia Inversionista' mentioned, unlike those for 'Rentista' or 'Pensionado' categories.
benefits: Allows permanent residency in Honduras from its inception, eliminating the need for frequent visa renewals or extensions of stay.
Opportunity to invest capital in various lawful economic activities or national financial instruments.
Spouse, minor children, dependent adult children, and parents can also obtain residency.
required_documents: Application addressed to the Secretary of State in the Offices of Human Rights, Justice, Governance, and Decentralization (or to the Executive Director of the National Institute of Migration).
Revenue stamps (timbres) of Lps. 100.00 per applicant.
Contact address and phone number of residence in Honduras.
Authenticated and endorsed Power of Attorney (Carta Poder) for legal representative, specifying their details and faculties.
Recent front-facing photograph (6cm x 5cm) with name on reverse for each applicant and dependant.
Original Certification of Migratory Movement, issued by the National Institute of Migration.
Original authorized entry application from a Honduran Consul, duly authenticated and legalized (if applying from abroad).
Certified clean criminal record from the country of origin and last residence, duly authenticated or apostilled.
Original certification of no police complaints or criminal records from the Honduran Dirección Policial de Investigación (DPI).
Medical certificate issued by a professional from the Honduran Medical College, no older than six months.
Authenticated and endorsed photocopy of the first page of the passport by a Public Notary.
Feasibility study and proposed investment schedule, detailing the investment amount.
Investment certificate.
Proof of application or registration in the Registry of Investors of the Secretariat of Industry and Commerce.
Constancia de Solvencia del Impuesto sobre la Renta (Income Tax Clearance) issued by the Servicio de Administración de Rentas (SAR).
All documents from abroad must be duly legalized/apostilled and officially translated into Spanish by the Ministry of Foreign Affairs or Honduran consulates.
application_process_steps: Prepare all required documents, ensuring foreign documents are legalized/apostilled and officially translated.
Submit the application to the Secretariat of State in the Offices of Human Rights, Justice, Governance, and Decentralization (or the National Institute of Migration) through a legal representative.
Provide proof of a minimum investment of USD $50,000 (or equivalent in HNL) and a guarantee deposit of USD $5,000 (or equivalent in HNL) to the Central Bank of Honduras.
Await the administrative resolution of the application.
Once approved, register with the National Registry of Foreigners at the National Institute of Migration.
Obtain the foreign resident identification card.

visas.name: Permiso Especial de Permanencia con Contrato de Trabajo / Residencia Temporal para Fines Laborales (Special Stay Permit with Work Contract / Temporary Residence for Working Purposes)
visas.description: This visa, officially known as 'Permiso Especial de Permanencia con Contrato de Trabajo' or 'Residencia Temporal para Fines Laborales', allows foreign nationals to reside and work legally in Honduras for periods exceeding three months. It is granted to individuals who have secured a job offer from a Honduran company and whose employment complies with local labor laws.
visas.target_applicant: The ideal applicant is a foreign national with a valid job offer from a Honduran employer, who will be responsible for initiating the application process and demonstrating compliance with labor regulations.
visas.path_to_residency_description: Individuals who have continuously held a Special Stay Permit for at least 5 years are eligible to apply for permanent residency.
visas.renewal_conditions: The permit can be renewed annually for up to 5 years, as long as the conditions of employment and legal status are maintained. For renewal, a photocopy of the previous work permit (carnet de trabajo), certification of resolution, and certification of inscription are required.
benefits: Legal authorization to work in Honduras.
Possibility of obtaining permanent residency after five years of continuous holding of the Special Stay Permit.
Access to a formal employment market in Honduras.
Employer sponsorship and support for the application process.
required_documents: Application addressed to the Executive Director of the National Institute of Migration, for each petitioner.
Authentic and legalized power of attorney (Carta Poder) if applying through a legal representative.
One recent passport-sized photograph (6x5 cm), with the applicant's name on the back.
Police clearance certificates from the country of origin and last residence, duly legalized.
Original certification from the Dirección Policial de Investigación (DPI) in Honduras stating no criminal record or complaints (for applicants over 18).
Medical certificate issued within six months prior to the application date.
Authenticated photocopy of the applicant's passport (all pages) with at least six months validity remaining.
Original employment contract issued by the private company, with signatures authenticated by a Notary.

Certification from the employer taking responsibility for the foreign worker's subsistence and exit from the country upon permit expiration, and committing to notify the National Institute of Migration of employment termination.

Certification from the Ministry of Labor and Social Security confirming the employer complies with Article 137 of the Constitution and Article 11 of the Labor Code (regarding the percentage of foreign workers, which cannot be less than 10% of the total workforce).
Accreditation of educational or professional qualifications (titles, diplomas, certificates), duly authenticated, demonstrating the applicant's capacity for the job.
Authenticated photocopy of the company's deed of incorporation or individual merchant declaration.
Authenticated photocopy of the company's current operating permit.
Certification from the Servicio de Administración de Rentas (SAR) confirming the company has commenced operations and is functioning.
Statement of results and balance sheet authorized by a certified accountant, with corresponding stamps and professional seal.
Payment receipts for corresponding fees.
Stamps required by law, to be affixed to the application and duly canceled.
All documents from abroad must be duly legalized (apostilled) and officially translated into Spanish if in another language.
application_process_steps: Enter Honduras (if not already in the country).
Obtain approval of the employment contract and a statement of compliance from the Ministry of Labor.
Prepare all required documents, ensuring all foreign documents are legalized/apostilled and officially translated into Spanish.
Submit the application to the National Institute of Migration (INM), generally through a legal representative, and pay the relevant fees.
Await temporary residence approval and notification of the resolution.
Proceed with registration, fingerprinting, and application for the residence card upon approval.

visas.name: Residencia por Vínculo Familiar (Family Reunification Visa)
visas.description: This visa program is for foreign nationals seeking to reside in Honduras based on a family relationship with a Honduran citizen or a resident foreigner. It allows for family reunification, enabling individuals to live legally in the country with their relatives.
visas.target_applicant: Ideal applicants include spouses, grandparents, parents, or siblings of Honduran citizens by birth, as well as economic dependents (spouses, minor children, adult dependent children, and parents) of foreigners who already hold a residency in Honduras.
visas.path_to_residency_description: Upon approval of the application, the applicant must register in the National Registry of Foreigners at the Instituto Nacional de Migración to obtain a resident identification card (carné de identificación de extranjero residente).
benefits: Legal right to reside in Honduras with family members.
Path to obtaining a resident identification card (carné de identificación de extranjero residente).
Promotes family unity and allows for long-term stay in the country.
required_documents: Application addressed to the Secretary of State in the Offices of Human Rights, Justice, Governance, and Decentralization.
Power of Attorney (Carta Poder) for legal representation.
Recent frontal photograph (6cm x 5cm), with the applicant's name on the back.
Document proving the family tie (e.g., marriage certificate, birth certificate).
Original certificate of migratory movement, issued by the Instituto Nacional de Migración.
Original criminal record certificate from the country of origin and last residence, duly authenticated/apostilled and officially translated if not in Spanish.
Certificate of no criminal complaints or police record from the Dirección Policial de Investigación (DPI) in Honduras.
Medical certificate (valid for no more than 6 months).
Authenticated photocopy of the first page of the passport.
Original entry application authorized by a Honduran Consul, duly authenticated and legalized (if applying from abroad). If the foreigner is already in Honduras, this is not necessary.
Timbres (stamps) of contracting.
Declaration of responsibility for the subsistence of dependents by the resident foreigner (for dependents of resident foreigners).
Documentation accrediting the marital union and/or economic dependence of the applicants (for spouses/dependents).
application_process_steps: Prepare all required documents, ensuring foreign documents are duly legalized/apostilled and officially translated into Spanish if needed.
Submit the application, addressed to the Secretary of State in the Offices of Human Rights, Justice, Governance, and Decentralization, through a legal representative (apoderado legal).
Pay the application fee and any required stamps (timbres).
Await the administrative resolution of the application.
Upon approval, proceed with registration in the National Registry of Foreigners at the Instituto Nacional de Migración.
Obtain the foreign resident identification card (carné de identificación de extranjero residente).

visas.name: Visa de Estudiante (Student Visa)
visas.description: The Visa de Estudiante (Student Visa) in Honduras is a Special Stay Permit ("Permiso Especial de Permanencia") granted to foreign nationals who wish to undertake studies or professional internships in educational institutions or organizations within Honduras. This permit allows for a legal temporary stay for the duration of their academic or professional program.
visas.target_applicant: Foreigners who have been admitted to an educational institution or professional internship program in Honduras.
visas.renewal_conditions: The permit is renewable annually upon payment of the corresponding fee and continued fulfillment of student status requirements and compliance with Honduran immigration laws.
benefits: Legal temporary residency in Honduras for the purpose of study or internship.
Access to Honduran educational institutions or professional training programs.
Permit is renewable annually, allowing for extended stays as needed for studies.
required_documents: Application addressed to the Executive Director of the National Migration Institute (INM), including contact address and phone number of the applicant and legal representative.
Legal stamps required by law, adhered to the application and duly canceled.
Document accrediting representation faculties (if applicable).
One recent photograph (6 cm high by 5 cm wide), front-facing, with the applicant's name on the back.
Criminal record certificate from the country of origin and last residence, duly legalized (apostilled or authenticated).
Original certificate from the Police Investigative Directorate (DPI) stating no complaints or criminal record, for applicants over eighteen (18) years of age.
Medical certificate issued no more than six (6) months prior to the application date.
Authenticated photocopy of the passport.

Proof of responsibility for the foreigner's subsistence during their stay and for their departure from the country upon expiration of the permit, and a commitment to notify the INM of the termination of their studies (as per Article 42 of the Migration and Foreigner Law Regulation).
If parents are responsible, they must present their foreign resident card.
For minors, authorization from both parents.
Admission letter or certificate issued by the institution where the foreigner will undertake studies or professional internship.
Proof of means of subsistence for the duration of the studies or professional internship; for minors, a commitment act from the natural or legal person responsible for their stay in the country.
Birth certificate, in case of being a minor.

All documents originating from abroad must be duly legalized (apostilled or authenticated) and officially translated into Spanish if not already in that language by the Secretariat of State in the Office of Foreign Affairs and International Cooperation or a Honduran Consulate.
application_process_steps: Gather all required documents, ensuring foreign documents are legalized/apostilled and officially translated into Spanish.
Prepare the application addressed to the Executive Director of the National Migration Institute (INM).
Adhere the necessary legal stamps to the application.
Submit the complete application package to the National Migration Institute (INM) in Honduras.
Pay the annual fee for the Special Stay Permit for Students.
Pay any additional fees for certifications, attestations, or supporting documents.

### Visas & Notes

- Work visa requires employer sponsorship
- Bay Islands expat community is well-established

Citizenship by Descent.desc: Citizenship by descent (Jus Sanguinis) is available to individuals born abroad to at least one Honduran parent who is a birthright national. This means children born abroad to naturalized Hondurans are generally excluded. Required documents typically include your birth certificate showing parentage, your Honduran parent's birth certificate and national ID (DNI), and registration documents if born abroad. All foreign documents usually need to be translated into Spanish and apostilled or authenticated.

Naturalization.desc: Naturalization is possible after meeting specific residency requirements. Foreigners who have resided in Honduras for three consecutive years may apply. This period is reduced to two years for Spanish or Ibero-American citizens and one year for nationals of other Central American states or foreigners sponsored by the government for agricultural, industrial, or scientific programs. Applicants must typically pass a test on the Honduran constitution, geography, and history. The National Congress can grant nationality for exceptional service to the nation. Naturalized citizens generally cannot hold more than one nationality unless a dual nationality treaty exists.

Birthright.desc: Honduras largely follows the principle of Jus Soli (right of soil). Birthright nationality applies to individuals born within Honduran territory, with the exception of children born to foreign diplomats. It also extends to persons born on Honduran warships, military planes, and commercial vessels in Honduran territorial waters, and foundlings discovered in the territory. While individuals born within the territory to foreign parents are generally granted citizenship, there can be exceptions, and specific cases may require individual assessment.

Spouse and Family.desc: Foreign citizens who marry a natural-born Honduran citizen may be eligible for naturalization. Historically, the residency requirement for spouses of Honduran nationals has seen preferential treatment, with some constitutions lowering it to one year. Currently, while marriage to a natural-born Honduran citizen is a recognized path to naturalization, it does not automatically grant nationality; a formal application and resolution are required. The nationality of a spouse or children is not automatically affected by marriage or its dissolution.

tax_advice:
*   **Territorial Tax System:** Honduras operates a territorial tax system, meaning residents are only taxed on income earned within Honduras. Foreign-sourced income, such as pensions, foreign investment income, or remote work income from foreign clients, is generally not subject to Honduran income tax.
*   **Personal Income Tax:** Residents are subject to progressive tax rates on Honduran-sourced income. As of 2024, the tax-exempt base for individuals is L 209,369.62 (approximately $8,477 USD) annually. An additional L 40,000 for medical or educational expenses can be added to the exempt base. The progressive rates are 15%, 20%, and 25% for higher income brackets.
*   **Corporate Income Tax (CIT):** The standard corporate income tax rate is 25% of net taxable income. A solidarity contribution surcharge of 5% applies to taxable income exceeding HNL 1 million, effectively bringing the top rate to 30%.
*   **Value Added Tax (VAT) / Sales Tax (ISV):** The standard sales tax rate is 15% on most goods and services. A higher rate of 18% applies to alcoholic beverages, tobacco, and certain luxury goods.
*   **Capital Gains Tax:** Capital gains are taxed at a flat rate of 10% on the net gain, applicable to the sale of real estate, shares, and other assets.
*   **Withholding Tax (WHT):** Payments from a Honduran resident to a non-resident for dividends, certain interest payments, rents, royalties, and management fees are subject to withholding tax at rates of 10% or 25%.
*   **Municipal Taxes:** All municipalities impose municipal taxes on corporations and individuals residing or doing business within the municipality, with specific formulas and incentives varying by locality.
*   **No Double Taxation Agreements:** Honduras currently does not have comprehensive double taxation agreements in force.
local_tips:
*   **Cost of Living:** Honduras offers a significantly lower cost of living than many Western countries. A comfortable lifestyle for a single person can range from $950 to $2,450 USD per month, depending on location and amenities. Roatán tends to be higher than mainland cities like Tegucigalpa or San Pedro Sula.
*   **Language:** Spanish is the official language. While English is spoken in tourist areas like the Bay Islands, learning basic Spanish is highly recommended for daily life and integration on the mainland.
*   **Safety:** Exercise a high degree of caution, especially after dark and in less affluent urban areas. Violent crime rates have decreased in recent years due to government efforts, but petty crime like theft and robbery remains common. Roatán and specific residential areas in Tegucigalpa (Lomas del Guijarro, Colonia Palmira, El Hatillo) and San Pedro Sula (Colonia Trejo, Los Andes) are generally considered safer for expats. Avoid traveling alone, using side roads, or accepting lifts from strangers.
*   **Registration & Residency:** Honduras offers several pathways to permanent residency, including Pensionado Visa (for retirees with $1,500/month pension), Rentista Visa (for those with $2,500/month passive income), Investor Visa ($50,000 minimum investment), and Bank Deposit Residency ($50,000 deposit in a Honduran bank account). All these routes can lead to eventual citizenship.
*   **Healthcare:** Private hospitals in major cities like Tegucigalpa (Hospital del Valle) and San Pedro Sula (Hospital CEMESA) offer good quality care, often with English-speaking staff. Public healthcare is underfunded. A standard private doctor consultation costs around $25-$40 USD.
*   **Utilities:** Electricity can be a significant monthly expense. Basic utilities for an 85m² apartment average around $120 per month, with internet adding about $44.
*   **Transportation:** Public transport costs are relatively low, with a monthly pass around $46. Be cautious using public transport or taxis and avoid travel after dark.
